recipes.name: Aloo Paratha
steps: Knead the atta with a pinch of salt and enough water into a soft dough, then cover and rest it for 15 minutes.
Boil, peel and mash the potatoes until no lumps remain.
Mix in chopped green chilli, grated ginger, coriander, salt, chilli powder, garam masala and amchur.
Roll a small disc of dough, set a ball of filling in the centre, pinch the edges shut and roll it gently into a round.
Cook on a hot tawa, flipping once, then brush both sides with ghee and press until golden spots appear.
Serve hot with curd, pickle or a little butter.

recipes.name: Anda Bhurji
steps: Melt the butter in a pan and soften the chopped onion and green chilli for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add chopped tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and salt, and cook until the tomato turns mushy.
Crack in the eggs and keep stirring on medium heat so they set into soft, moist curds.
Sprinkle garam masala and coriander, take the pan off the heat while the eggs are still slightly soft, and serve with toasted pav.

recipes.name: Besan Chilla
steps: Whisk the besan with salt, turmeric, chilli powder and ajwain, adding water little by little to get a smooth, pourable batter.
Stir in finely chopped onion, tomato, green chilli and coriander.
Grease a hot tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread it thin with the back of the ladle.
Drizzle oil around the edges, cook until the underside is golden, then flip and cook the other side.
Serve hot with green chutney or ketchup.

recipes.name: Gobi Paratha
steps: Knead the atta with a pinch of salt and water into a soft dough and keep it covered for 15 minutes.
Grate the cauliflower finely, sprinkle a little salt, wait 10 minutes and squeeze out the water it releases.
Mix the gobi with green chilli, ginger, ajwain, coriander, chilli powder and garam masala; add the rest of the salt just before stuffing.
Stuff a portion into a rolled disc of dough, seal the edges and roll it out carefully.
Roast on a hot tawa with ghee on both sides until crisp and brown-spotted.
Serve with curd, pickle or butter.

recipes.name: Idli Sambar
steps: Grease the idli moulds, fill each with batter and steam for 10 to 12 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Pressure-cook the toor dal with turmeric until very soft, then mash it well.
Soak the tamarind in warm water for 10 minutes and squeeze out the pulp.
Boil the shallots, drumstick pieces and chopped tomato with the tamarind pulp, sambar powder and salt until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the mashed dal, thin it with water to a pouring consistency and simmer for 5 minutes.
Splutter mustard seeds, hing and curry leaves in hot oil, pour over the sambar, add coriander and serve with the idlis.

recipes.name: Masala Dosa
steps: Boil, peel and roughly crumble the potatoes.
Heat oil, splutter the mustard seeds, then add curry leaves, green chilli, ginger and sliced onion; cook until the onion is soft.
Add turmeric, salt and the potatoes with a splash of water, mix well and cook for 3 minutes to make the filling.
Spread a ladle of batter into a thin circle on a hot greased tawa and drizzle oil around the edge.
When the dosa is crisp and golden underneath, place a spoonful of potato filling in the middle and fold it over.
Serve at once with chutney or sambar.

recipes.name: Methi Thepla
steps: Wash the methi leaves well and chop them finely.
In a bowl mix atta, methi, curd, grated ginger, chopped green chilli, sesame seeds, turmeric, chilli powder, salt and a tablespoon of oil.
Knead into a firm but smooth dough using very little water, and rest it for 10 minutes.
Roll small balls of dough into thin rounds, dusting with atta as needed.
Cook each thepla on a hot tawa with a little oil on both sides until light brown spots appear.
Eat warm with pickle or curd, or pack them for travel since they stay soft for a day or two.

recipes.name: Moong Dal Chilla
steps: Soak the moong dal for 3 to 4 hours or overnight, then drain.
Grind it with ginger, green chilli and a little water into a smooth, thick batter, then mix in salt, jeera and hing.
Stir in finely chopped onion and coriander.
Spread a ladle of batter thinly on a hot greased tawa, drizzle oil around it and cook until the base turns golden.
Flip, cook the other side for a minute and serve with green chutney.

recipes.name: Onion Uttapam
steps: Finely chop the onion, green chilli, ginger and coriander and toss them with a pinch of salt.
Heat a greased tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread it into a thick round about the size of a small plate.
Scatter the onion mixture evenly on top and press it lightly into the batter.
Drizzle oil around the edges, cover and cook on medium heat until the base is golden.
Flip, cook the topping side for 1 to 2 minutes and serve with coconut chutney or sambar.

recipes.name: Paneer Paratha
steps: Knead the atta with a pinch of salt and water into a soft dough; cover and rest it for 15 minutes.
Crumble the paneer and mix it with finely chopped onion, green chilli, ginger, coriander, chilli powder, garam masala and salt.
Roll out a disc of dough, place the filling in the centre, bring the edges together and seal.
Flatten and roll it gently into a round without letting the filling break through.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee on both sides until golden and crisp at the edges.
Serve hot with curd or pickle.

recipes.name: Kanda Poha
steps: Rinse the poha in a strainer under running water for a few seconds, drain and leave it to soften.
Heat oil and fry the peanuts until crunchy, then lift them out.
In the same oil splutter mustard seeds, then add curry leaves, green chilli, chopped onion and diced potato; cook until the potato is tender.
Add turmeric, salt and a pinch of sugar, fold in the poha gently and cook covered on low heat for 2 to 3 minutes.
Mix in the peanuts and lemon juice, and top with coriander and sev.

recipes.name: Puri Bhaji
steps: Knead the atta with a little salt, a spoon of oil and water into a stiff dough; rest it for 10 minutes.
Boil and peel the potatoes, then break them into rough chunks by hand.
Heat a little oil, add jeera and hing, then ginger, green chilli and chopped tomato; cook until soft.
Add turmeric, chilli and coriander powders, salt, the potatoes and a cup of water; simmer 8 to 10 minutes until the gravy thickens a little.
Roll small rounds of dough and deep-fry them one at a time in hot oil, pressing gently so they puff up.
Serve the hot puris with the aloo bhaji and a sprinkle of coriander.

recipes.name: Sabudana Khichdi
steps: Rinse the sabudana two or three times and soak it in just enough water to cover for 5 to 6 hours; drain well so the pearls squash easily.
Dry-roast the peanuts, rub off the skins and pound them coarsely.
Toss the peanut powder, salt and sugar through the sabudana.
Heat ghee, add jeera, curry leaves, green chilli and small potato cubes, and cook covered until the potato is soft.
Add the sabudana mixture and stir gently on low heat for 5 to 7 minutes until the pearls turn translucent.
Finish with lemon juice and coriander and serve warm.

recipes.name: Rava Upma
steps: Dry-roast the sooji on low heat until it smells nutty but is still pale, then tip it onto a plate.
Heat ghee, splutter mustard seeds, then add cashews, curry leaves, ginger, green chilli and chopped onion; saute until the onion softens.
Pour in about 2 1/2 cups of water with the salt and bring it to a rolling boil.
Lower the heat and add the sooji in a thin stream, stirring all the time so no lumps form.
Cover and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the water is absorbed, fluff it up, add coriander and serve hot.

recipes.name: Vegetable Daliya
steps: Dry-roast the daliya with a teaspoon of ghee for 3 to 4 minutes until lightly golden.
In a pressure cooker heat the remaining ghee, add jeera, then onion, ginger and green chilli, and saute until soft.
Add chopped tomato, diced carrot and peas with turmeric and salt, and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the daliya and about 3 cups of water, stir and pressure-cook for 2 whistles.
Let the pressure drop on its own, loosen the daliya with a spoon and garnish with coriander.
